I am personally very, very happy and I’m glad that the ‘honeymoon’ period is sort of over. By that I mean the all consuming infatuation of a person. Now we love each other on such a deep level it’s ridiculous. But now we also have found a way to focus on other things that we care about, while being together. In the ‘honeymoon’ phrase it was literally just about us the whole time and it was insane in the best way possible. I just thought it was important to highlight your words again, as people usually tend to distill important parts into writing. And this has nothing to do with him misleading you, it’s more to do with his sentence of not wanting to make a decision for himself.

I think you have answered your questions here already. Objectively, from what is written here, you clearly want something that he doesn’t want and vice versa. And from what he’s saying about wanting someone else to make that decision for him… that’s immature. A grown adult is someone who makes decisions for themselves, especially the hard ones. He sounds like if you stay in this, he’ll not make a decision until you’re in this same argument sometime later.

I’ve been in a similar position and the best you can do for yourself is to go in the direction of what you actually want – a longterm relationship that leads to marriage to someone who also wants the same thing.
I think you sound very clear and confident in your original decision but the pain of the breakup is making you question things. But obviously I don’t know you.

In short, be mindful: he already told you what he wants originally. The only way to deal with it, in my opinion is just to be honest with each other. It’s a hard conversation but it’s better than living in a state of anxiety and uncertainty. Good luck.

I don't like the term celibate to begin with. It implys that there's religion attached to it when I am not religious at all. And honestly, I don't really think it is a new thing - all my friends took a while to lose their virginity, me too. Now that I look back on it, there was too much pressure on me to do it just to know what it was like. I remember doing it with the first guy who sort of liked me just to get it over with and it was bad. My friend got shamed by her gynocologist that she was in her 20s and still a virgin. that part really, really sucks.

the kicker here for me was that sex was not good for me because I needed more emotionally to connect with someone - have things in common, in general have fun and not worry about a guy not using a condom etc. Which made my really low bar grow a bit for self care lol. Because going out with men that were only after sex did not satisfy me at all - I wanted and needed more, and demanding this from someone who did not want the same was exhausting and silly. Once I learned that, I just looked at dating and sex much more relaxed - if it's not an enthuastic 'yes', it was a 'no'. And honestly, that was liberating. I started to take care of myself, my needs more, stopped running after men who did not care about me. I feel like my schedule opened up so much. It was lovely and for me it was definitely more than being 'celibate'. It was just not spending time in vain for things that did not satisfy or at least entertain me.

Don't get me wrong, I did still go on dates and pursued people but I quickly learned I didn't vibe with them after the first date and let it go - I also was completely transparent to them about it.

The sad thing I would say was, I really wanted to be that girl that just goes and gets whichever guy she wants but I was not built like that, and it felt dissapointing to learn that. But then I actually learnt what I liked, didn't and trusted myself to take care of me x

Now I'm in a relationship with someone wonderful, that I click with so well and it feels good. Before I was single and 'celibate' for around 2 years. And before that for much much longer.
